name: Federal Infrastructure Payments Advanced Part 1
description:
This is a TWO PART LAW. (1/2)

This is a utility law which covers automated payments for most road work and other infrastructure projects; And applies gaurdrails for roadworkers. The title %Federal Engineer% allows bypassing placement gaurdrails. However, this law does not restrict the building of ports or laser towers to engineers. Additionally the government retains the option to supplement these payments or pay for some projects differently. Nor should any provision herein be taken to replace or restrict any minister in how they choose to complete their duties. 


=====================================
USAGE ADVICE FOR MOIS
=====================================
This law includes two extra districts related to paying for roads. The first is [Highway Work Bonus], when this district overlaid on the [National Highway] digging or tree removal has its payments doubled, this does not work outside the main highway districts. 
The second district is [Federal Arterial] this district will pay for digging and road placement outside of the national highways, it is largely intended to pay for connection roads to link settlements to the highway but may be useful in other situations, it should not be placed over the main highway districts to prevent double payments.

The MoI and PM are given several extra government accounts labeled {#National Infrastructure Payout (XYZ)}, each account defines the respective payout for a given tier of materials or action, and should contain exactly the amount to be paid per instance. Actual payments will be made from the main MoI budget.
If you wish to pay extra for certain block types that is best done by passing an extra law which will make the payments additive to the standard payout, note when doing that, this law will still control placement permissions and they do not need duplicated in the new one.

Payouts for placing blocks +T4 [Laser Towers] and [Federal Ports] are provided, however only %Federal Engineer% is paid for digging. This should be coordinated with other government branches to ensure people are not getting double paid. Engineers are also paid for placing roads in the buffer districts.

This law features six districts for controlling road height, five [Height (XYZ)] districts and [Highway Ramps], these districts should be on a separate district map from [Federal Work Bonus]. Outside of these districts the law will assume the default height of Y=75 and apply payments and restrictions based on that. 
Overlaying a section of [National Highway] with a [Height (XYZ)] applies payments and restrictions altered as appropriate for that height. These heights can be changed by editing the law (see documentation), but by default are 69, 72, 78, 81, 84.
The district [Highway Ramps] is used to define where changes in height should occur. As a rule of thumb you will need one plot length of [Highway Ramps] for every block of height change in the road. These changes should be infrequent and never within two plots of an intersection.
Work in [Highway Ramps] is restricted to %Federal Engineers% as they can not be given gaurdrails


=====================================
TECHNICAL DOCUMENTATION
=====================================
The law assumes [SC] National Highways Legislation is active and already restricts interactions to those titled %Federal Highway Worker%
This law is usually paired with 'Federal Infrastructure Regulations' but will function without it.
This law is a fork of 'Federal Infrastructure Payments' this version adds support for multiple road heights but should otherwise be identical.

This law requires the districts [Federal Arterial], [Federal Work Bonus], [Height 69], [Height 72], [Height 78], [Height 81], [Height 84], and [Highway Ramps].
[Federal Arterial] and [Federal Work Bonus] should be placed on a separate district map from the height and ramp districts.
The following government accounts set to be managed by PM and MoI are also required, {#National Infrastructure Payout (Tamping)}, {#National Infrastructure Payout (Buffer Gravel)}, {#National Infrastructure Payout (Tree Chop)}
These lists do not include references supplied by the server setup import.

Changing the road height requires changing the value in the first if block for sections: 1 (Road Height Settings), 4 (Digging Payments), 5 (Buffer Gravel Payments), 6 (Tamping Payments). The default road height should be the first sub-if block listed and will be paired with a 'outside all' district check for the height variation districts. The height districts can be changed in the same way in their respective sub-if blocks. Section 8 (Digging Payments) has a second set of heights defined in the else-if, this controls how high above road height digging is paid for but does not prevent digging higher. This is typically the road height plus 7, but can be changed independently.

Full Documentation: https://discord.com/channels/254025510651297802/1544685594251104276

properties.Title: Road Height Settings
properties.UserDescription: This section controls road placement height in the 'Federal Highways' districts. 'Highway Ramps' district restricts placements to engineers only since they can not be gaurdrailed. If no 'Height Y' district is present the default height is set to 75. 'Height Y' districts are by default 69, 72, 78, 81, 84; but the MoI or PM may request they be changed as needed per cycle.

properties.Title: Digging payment
properties.UserDescription:
Digging bellow highways (standard height 75) is prevented to avoid issues with vehicles to sinking below the ground.

For tunnels under mounten a payment equal to the account holding for mining is made to dig out drivable space. Tunnel height should be at least 6 clear blocks high, to allow all verhicles that are drivable to pass through it. Plus an additional block for a tunnel lining.

A bonus payment is offered in areas districted by the Minister of Infrastructure or Prime Minister for areas that need extra attention.

properties.Title: Buffer Gravel Payments
properties.UserDescription:
Set rules for which gravel and dirt placements are allowed within the highway buffer districts.

The Minister of Infrastructure sets the ammount that is to be payout out for placing gravels or dirt in the buffer zone. (Used to fill in low spots or smooth the terrain.)
